messages:
laura: Heads-up — we're about to rotate a Key Vault key used for envelope encryption across two tenants. want to sync on RBAC vs access policy implications and audit log gaps.
sam: thanks. which key? customer-data-prod-encryptor in /subscriptions/..../rg/security/kv-main ?
jin: yep that's the one. current setup: service principal in customer tenant A has access via access policy. we're moving to managed identity in tenant B and trying RBAC assignments instead.
rachel: is this the one that does DEK wrapping for S3 uploads? envelope encryption with AWS KMS DEKs stored encrypted by AKV KEK?
jin: correct. flow: app calls AKV wrapKey -> returns ciphertext for DEK -> store to S3 metadata. on read: unwrapKey -> decrypt DEK -> decrypt object.
laura: constraints: 1) can't break live decrypts, 2) audit trail must show which principal requested unwraps for compliance, 3) cross-tenant access will be short-lived during migration.
mike: big gotcha: AKV access policies only work in the vault's tenant. cross-tenant service principal won't be honored by access-policies. RBAC (Key Vault Data Plane RBAC) supports Azure AD principals from other tenants only via guest accounts/federation, but requires AAD guest/service-principal setup.
sam: so options: A) federate the app identity into the KV tenant as guest/service-principal and use RBAC; B) temporarily provision a service principal in the KV tenant, backfill credentials; C) switch to a proxy service in KV tenant that performs wrap/unwrap and exposes a narrow internal API.
laura: tradeoffs: A minimal long-term, but onboarding guests needs org agreement + audit; B quick but credentials lifecycle + rotation pain; C adds network surface and needs strict rate limits and OIDC mTLS.
jin: question about rotation sequence: we need to rotate KEK (AKV key) without losing ability to unwrap old DEKs. recommended approach = create new key version, set as 'current' for new wraps, keep old key versions and allow unwrap until we rewrap old DEKs. rewrap plan: iterate objects and rewrap DEKs opportunistically, or run offline rewrap job. any audit implications?
rachel: audit: make sure Purview/Log Analytics picks up KeyVaultAuditEvent for Unwrap/Wrap and that the logs include authenticationPrincipalName. RBAC path gives principal info in logs; access policies might show applicationId but less friendly. confirm with SIEM.
laura: can we rely on 'soft' unwrap with key versions? i.e., unwrap with new key version won't work for old ciphertexts. have to pass correct key version or let vault select if you call unwrapKey on key name without version?
jin: unwrapKey on a key name will try latest key version unless you specify version. ciphertext created with a previous version contains metadata? Azure's wrapKey output doesn't contain bit of metadata pointing to version by default. we store the wrapped DEK ciphertext only. So recommended: when wrapping, record the keyVersion used in metadata alongside ciphertext. that way unwrap job can pick correct key version.
sam: yup we store `kv_key: key-name`, `kv_key_version: 2024-09-12T...` in the object metadata. if not present, we attempt to brute-force by trying known versions in descending order, but that's messy.
mike: audit log gap: when we migrate to RBAC, make sure Diagnostic Settings on the vault send 'Microsoft.KeyVault/OperationalLogs' and 'AuditEvent' to our central Log Analytics workspace BEFORE swapping identities. we had an incident where diag settings were accidentally scoped to subscription and a gap occurred. sec-oncall-bot: Incident guardrail: if unwrap failures exceed 0.5% in 10m window, open P0 channel and run the unwrap-fallback-service.
rachel: vuln triage note: we found CVE-2024-xxxxx in client SDK with wrapKey padding edge-case. patch to sdk vX.Y.Z fixed it. ensure all our services use patched SDK before mass rewrap.
laura: ok action list: - @jin add key_version metadata write to uploader (if missing) - @sam add diagnostic settings to vault -> LA workspace and ensure retention policy 365d - @mike run a dry-run rewrap job on a small bucket and report unwrap error rate - @rachel verify SDK versions in build matrix and block releases with vulnerable dep.
jin: one more: RBAC vs access policies migration: to migrate safely, enable Data Plane RBAC on vault (preview flag in some regions back then) and set permissions for 'Key Vault Crypto User' roles for the managed identity. test unwrap permissions via `az rest` impersonating the identity.
sam: command snippet I used for testing: ```bash
# as a test user (guest svc principal) get token
TOKEN=$(az account get-access-token --resource https://vault.azure.net --query accessToken -o tsv)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -X POST "https://{vault-name}.vault.azure.net/keys/{key-name}/unwrap?api-version=7.4" \
  -d '{"alg":"RSA-OAEP","value":"<base64cipher>"}'
```
laura: good. also note: if tenant boundary requires service principal re-creation, rotation windows must match CI/CD release windows. we'll need runbook steps for rollback (re-add old principal or toggle proxy).
mike: I'll draft a runbook snippet and add circuit-breaker checks. also add an automated replay of audit logs into the incident channel when we see >= 3 failed unwraps from same principal.
rachel: compliance ask: preserve key rotation history and exportable ledger for auditors. Enable purge protection and soft-delete on vault. keep KeyRotationPolicy object and rotation schedule in infra as code (tfstate + docs).
jin: timeline proposal: 1) today: enable diag logging, patch SDKs, add metadata write 2) this week: create new key version and start canary rewrap on test bucket 3) next week: broad rewrap with throttling and monitoring 4) after 30d: revoke old key versions if no unwraps observed and after compliance sign-off.
laura: approve. please update runbook PR and tag me. if anything shows >1% unwrap failures revert to proxy pattern.
sec-oncall-bot: Reminder scheduled: key-rotation-check runbook job will execute in 24h and post results. :bell:
sam: thanks everyone — i'll paste the diag setting commands and a small terraform snippet into the runbook PR in a bit.
laura: perfect, let's keep the migration in a single thread. post PR links here when ready. :thumbsup:
